encoding_choice.chosen: a line-class grammar expressed in JSON
encoding_choice.why: Every rule §14.2 makes decidable is a statement about a LINE — its class, its token shapes, and whether its class is admitted on the surface at all. A JSON Schema describes a data structure; the artifact these emitters produce is text, and the thing being constrained is the text. Expressing line classes directly means an emitter validates what it is about to print rather than a model of it, which is the distinction §14.2's own AC3 rests on.
encoding_choice.declined: JSON Schema — checkable by tooling already present in this repository (checks/check-terrain-composition.sh validates survey records against survey-schema.json), but it would require modelling rendered Markdown and terminal text as a document tree first, and that model would itself be an unchecked restatement of the format.
encoding_choice.recorded_here_because: SPEC.md §14.1 names this file and its duties and deliberately does not decide the encoding (story 1.52 SQ1). A choice made in implementation and left unwritten is one the next editor re-derives.

LessonDisplayID.means: a member's owner-facing display id, assigned once in the survey record (§14.3)
LessonDisplayID.producer: terrain/terrain.mjs cmdSurvey — minted ONCE per candidate in the survey record (§14.3), resolved at render time by displayIdOf(); story 1.53, kogaki#345
LessonDisplayID.absence_is_abnormal: A member whose survey record predates §14.3 carries no display_id. The surfaces render NO_DISPLAY_ID and state the abnormality; they NEVER substitute the slug, because the slug is what §14.3 removes and a silent fallback would undo the decision while looking like robustness. So an owner surface may carry the NO_DISPLAY_ID token in a LessonDisplayID position, and a refusal built to admit only ^L[0-9]+$ there would reject exactly the legacy record the abnormality exists to make visible.

cotag_screen.indentation_is_not_a_carrier: v3, kogaki#317. NO LINE CLASS ON THIS SURFACE ENCODES LEADING WHITESPACE, and that is a contract rather than a formatting preference. Indentation was the sole carrier of subordination through v2, and the 2026-08-09 hands-on round found it unreadable for the reason it cannot fix: claim lines are long prose, they wrap at the terminal edge, and a wrapped continuation begins at column 0 — so the hierarchy disappears exactly where the text is longest. The level now rides tokens.GroupID and tokens.SubGroupID, which survive wrapping because they are content. A future edit re-introducing leading spaces to signal level is re-introducing the defect.
cotag_screen.line_class_allowlist_went_inert_here_in_: RESOLVED in the same v3, and kept as a record rather than deleted. The flush-left change removed the six-space indent that was `group_prose`'s only constraint, so the class began admitting every line and `decidable_rules.expressible.line_class_allowlist` — LIVE on this surface through v2 — had no unadmitted line left to find. It was found by the suite going red on the spec diff alone, not by review of the change, and the alternative preview shown at the deciding gate described the new appearance without naming this cost. The repair is `group_prose`'s `> ` marker above (owner decision 2026-08-11). reader_notes.form_notation_tolerances: Three tolerances the story-1.54 predicate applies when reading a `form`, declared here because a reader comparing the grammar to the code would otherwise find them only in terrain/format-guard.mjs. (1) A LEADING `\n` denotes the blank line before the class, not two characters of it — the emitters separate blocks with `\n`-prefixed strings and this file transcribes them as written; the blank itself is the `blank` class. (2) A form containing `…` is matched as a PREFIX, because the ellipsis abbreviates the rest of a long fixed line; anchoring the tail would make the abbreviation STRICTER than the text it abbreviates, which is the `preamble` and `judged_empty_notice` defect in another costume. (3) TRAILING whitespace is admitted, because a Markdown hard break is two trailing spaces and this notation cannot write them; the identity block emits three such lines. None of the three admits a token, class or line this file does not already admit.
reader_notes.line_class_allowlist_is_inert_on_full_re:

WIDENED, NOT REPAIRED, AT v6 (kogaki#472). The neighborhood section's classes land on this surface and most are CONSTRAINED — the suggestion row's three lines, the counts line, the over-cap refusal's two. (Refreshed at kogaki#686: the earlier example set named the bound line and the per-family figures, two classes that ruling deletes, in the one note a reader consults to learn what the green suite does NOT cover.) They inherit the inertness anyway, and the mechanism is `class_matching_is_by_specificity`: a MALFORMED neighborhood row fails its own specific class, falls through to `group_claim_body`, and is admitted. So the exemption is a property of the SURFACE, caused by three classes and reaching every class on it, including classes added long after the three were written. 

STATED AT THE WIDENING RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER, because that is what the served position asks of exactly this act: 'When a rule carries an exception justified by one member's genuine constraint and the rule's scope is later widened, the exception travels with it onto members that never had the constraint -- and because an exception exists precisely in order to skip a check, its wrongful inheritance emits no error, no warning and no failing test, so re-derive every exception at every widening and withdraw it unless the new member can state the original justification in its own terms.' (consulted: product-lab@8906f20752e27d1935c62f24c8ba41ea1d55dba0 LESSONS.md:64, an-inherited-exemption-signals-nothing). The neighborhood classes CANNOT state the original justification in their own terms -- they are not claim bodies and nothing about them needs a free-form form -- so by that line the exemption is owed a withdrawal, and this note records that it was NOT withdrawn here. What blocks the withdrawal is unchanged and is the note's own first paragraph: constraining the three body classes is a decision about this artifact and belongs on its own issue, and kogaki#472's licence names the amendment, not that decision. 

What v6 buys anyway, so the coverage claim is not read as empty: the classes are DECLARED, so `no_element_names` and `pin_once_per_file` reach the section, the golden fixture (SPEC §14.5) exercises its forms — the specimen landed with kogaki#473 (story 1.69), discharging the owed tense this phrase carried across the spec-ahead-of-code interval, and a renderer edit that changes a form now diverges from a written contract instead of from nothing at all. reader_notes.class_matching_is_by_specificity: Classes are matched most-specific-first, specificity being the count of literal non-space characters a form pins outside its placeholders — not declaration order. `group_prose` (`      <composer prose>`) admits every six-space-indented line including every `subgroup_heading`, so first-match-wins classified subgroup headings as prose and `subgroup_members_sum_to_parent` summed zero and refused a conformant screen. Order would have fixed that case and left the next one silent: a class added in the wrong place shadows another and nothing says so.

precedence_is_per_axis: THIS FILE WINS ON THE RENDERED FORM AND ON NOTHING ELSE. §14.1 makes it authoritative over what an owner surface's text may look like — the BUILT axis. It is NOT authoritative over what was DECIDED: where an entry records an owner ruling, the ruling's home is the issue named beside it and this file carries a POINTER, not the verdict. Written down because the two halves are answered by different systems and one rule for both hands this file the last word on facts it cannot observe (consulted: product-lab@4cc496b39be1d7641aaaaf678668fb64eda35f17 gloss/lessons/knowledge-architecture.md:227 — 'Say which system decides which half'). Added after PR #352 round 1 recorded consultation-map entry 3 UNCOVERED for the second consecutive PR on this chain; the consult that entry prescribes is what produced this paragraph, and the first thing it found was that the entries below had been written in the wrong voice.

deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.what_is_owed: A decision on whether full_report's three bare-placeholder body classes (`group_claim_body`, `subgroup_claim_body`, `member_gloss_body`) are constrained, so that `line_class_allowlist` becomes live on this surface -- or whether a SECTIONED allowlist is admitted instead, refusing only lines under a heading whose section declares a closed class set. The second shape would make the rule live for the neighborhood section without touching the claim bodies at all.
deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.why_it_is_a_decision_and_not_a_fix: Both shapes change what the emit-time refusal REJECTS, which is the artifact's contract with every producer and every fixture. Constraining a claim body decides what a composer may write; a sectioned allowlist introduces a second scoping axis to a file whose whole precedence argument rests on one. Neither is settled by reading the code, so it is owed on its own licensing issue with alternatives and a receipt BEFORE any predicate embeds an answer.
deferred_slot_full_report_allowlist.not_filed_here: Filing it now would be `conditional-on:` shaped -- its validity turns on which shape a future sitting takes -- and SPEC-issue-creation refuses that filing, folding it into the deciding issue's acceptance items instead. Named here so the slot is visible rather than rediscovered.
